basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 23.' and it opens '| Vers. 23. Hoc nunc os ex ossibus meis. Adam videns mulierem sibi simillimam ex omnibus'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 23. Hoc nunc os ex ossibus meis. Adam videns mulierem sibi simillimam ex omnibus creaturis recognovit eam ex suae carnis substantia formatam, vel etiam, ut B. Augustinus dicit, factus Adam in exstasi mentis et prophetiae spiritu afflatus scivit costam sibi subductam et mulierem formatam. Vocabitur virago.--Virago a viro est dicta, sicut et in Hebraeis is, vir dicitur, et deinde issa derivatum, id est mulier. Ex hoc Israel etiam compositum est.
